# Adding New Source Files to the Object Detection Build

## Context

The project at `hailo_apps/cpp/object_detection/` uses **CMake** as its build system.
Running CMake produces a generated `Makefile` inside `build/aarch64/`. The header of
that file reads:

```
# CMAKE generated file: DO NOT EDIT!
# Generated by "Unix Makefiles" Generat7or, CMake Version 3.31
```

This means **you must never edit `build/aarch64/Makefile` by hand**. Any manual edit
is overwritten the next time CMake runs. The correct place to declare sources,
include paths, and link libraries is `CMakeLists.txt`.

---

## New Files Added

Three new translation units were placed in the source directory:

| File | Purpose | Extra dependency |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `rasp_gpio.cpp` / `.h` | Raspberry Pi GPIO control via `libgpiod` | `gpiod` |
| `RPLidar_S2L.cpp` / `.h` | RPLidar S2L driver (serial communication + scan parsing) | RPLidar SDK (`libsl_lidar_sdk.a`) |
| `spike.cpp` / `.h` | LEGO Spike Prime serial interface | none (standard C headers only) |

Also present but header-only: `common_var.h` (shared type definitions used by the above).

---

## Why CMake Didn't Pick Them Up Automatically

`CMakeLists.txt` uses a glob to collect sources:

```cmake
file(GLOB SOURCES
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/*.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/utils/*.cpp"
)
```

CMake evaluates globs **at configure time** (when you run `cmake`), not at build time
(when you run `make`). The build directory was configured before the new `.cpp` files
existed, so the generated `Makefile` had no knowledge of them. Simply dropping files
into the source folder is not enough — CMake must be re-run.

---

## Dependency Analysis

### `rasp_gpio.cpp`

The header includes:

```cpp
#include <gpiod.h>
```

This requires the `libgpiod` development package (present on the system:
`libgpiod-dev:arm64 2.2.1-2+deb13u1`) and linking against `-lgpiod`.

### `RPLidar_S2L.cpp`

The header includes:

```cpp
#include <sl_lidar.h>
#include <sl_lidar_driver.h>
```

These headers and the pre-built static library live inside the project:

```
object_detection/rplidar_sdk/
├── sdk/
│   ├── include/      ← headers (sl_lidar.h, sl_lidar_driver.h, …)
│   └── src/          ← internal SDK source headers
└── output/Linux/Release/
    └── libsl_lidar_sdk.a   ← pre-built static library
```

### `spike.cpp`

Uses only standard C headers (`stdio.h`, `stdlib.h`, `termios.h`, etc.).
No additional link libraries are required.

---

## Changes Made to `CMakeLists.txt`

Two sections were modified.

### 1. RPLidar SDK variables + include directories

**Before:**

```cmake
# ============================================================
# Include dirs
# ============================================================
target_include_directories(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    ${OpenCV_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/utils
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../common"
)
```

**After:**

```cmake
# ============================================================
# RPLidar SDK
# ============================================================
set(RPLIDAR_SDK_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/rplidar_sdk")
set(RPLIDAR_LIB "${RPLIDAR_SDK_DIR}/output/Linux/Release/libsl_lidar_sdk.a")

# ============================================================
# Include dirs
# ============================================================
target_include_directories(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    ${OpenCV_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/utils
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../common"
    "${RPLIDAR_SDK_DIR}/sdk/include"
    "${RPLIDAR_SDK_DIR}/sdk/src"
)
```

Two new include paths are added so the compiler can find `<sl_lidar.h>` and the
internal SDK headers used by the driver.

### 2. Link libraries

**Before:**

```cmake
target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    HailoRT::libhailort
    Threads::Threads
    ${OpenCV_LIBS}
    yaml-cpp
    CURL::libcurl
)
```

**After:**

```cmake
target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    HailoRT::libhailort
    Threads::Threads
    ${OpenCV_LIBS}
    yaml-cpp
    CURL::libcurl
    ${RPLIDAR_LIB}
    gpiod
)
```

`${RPLIDAR_LIB}` expands to the full path of the pre-built static library.
`gpiod` links the system `libgpiod` shared library.

---

## Regenerating the Makefile

After saving `CMakeLists.txt`, CMake must be re-run from the build directory:

```bash
cd hailo_apps/cpp/object_detection/build/aarch64
cmake ../..
```

CMake re-evaluates the glob, discovers the three new `.cpp` files, incorporates the
new include paths and link libraries, and writes a fresh `Makefile`.

---

## Verification

After regeneration, the following command confirms all expected translation units are
registered:

```bash
grep -o "object_detection.dir/[^ ]*\.cpp" \
  CMakeFiles/object_detection.dir/build.make | sort -u
```

Output:

```
object_detection.dir/home/maker/hailo-apps/hailo_apps/cpp/common/hailo_infer.cpp
object_detection.dir/home/maker/hailo-apps/hailo_apps/cpp/common/resources_manager.cpp
object_detection.dir/home/maker/hailo-apps/hailo_apps/cpp/common/toolbox.cpp
object_detection.dir/object_detection.cpp
object_detection.dir/rasp_gpio.cpp
object_detection.dir/RPLidar_S2L.cpp
object_detection.dir/spike.cpp
object_detection.dir/utils/utils.cpp
```

`rasp_gpio.cpp`, `RPLidar_S2L.cpp`, and `spike.cpp` are now part of the build.

---

## Building

```bash
cd hailo_apps/cpp/object_detection/build/aarch64
make -j$(nproc)
```

The resulting executable is placed in the build directory as `object_detection`.

---

## Rule for Future New Files

- **`.cpp` files** dropped into `object_detection/` are picked up automatically by the
  existing glob — just re-run `cmake ../..` from the build directory.
- **New external libraries** (headers + link targets) must be declared in
  `CMakeLists.txt` under `target_include_directories` and `target_link_libraries`
  before re-running CMake.
- **Never edit** `build/aarch64/Makefile` directly.
